messages.subject: [R-pkg-team] Bug#955561: src:r-cran-rmarkdown: fails to migrate to testing for too long
messages.subject_clean: [R-pkg-team] Bug#955561: src:r-cran-rmarkdown: fails to migrate to testing for too long
messages.body_plain:
Source: r-cran-rmarkdown
Version: 1.15+dfsg-1
Severity: serious
Control: fixed -1 2.1+dfsg-1
Tags: sid bullseye
User: release.debian.org at packages.debian.org
Usertags: out-of-sync

Dear maintainer(s),

As recently announced [1], the Release Team now considers packages that
are out-of-sync between testing and unstable for more than 60 days as
having a Release Critical bug in testing. Your package
src:r-cran-rmarkdown in its current version in unstable has been trying
to migrate for 66 days [2]. Hence, I am filing this bug.

If a package is out of sync between unstable and testing for a longer
period, this usually means that bugs in the package in testing cannot be
fixed via unstable. Additionally, blocked packages can have impact on
other packages, which makes preparing for the release more difficult.
Finally, it often exposes issues with the package and/or
its (reverse-)dependencies. We expect maintainers to fix issues that
hamper the migration of their package in a timely manner.

This bug will trigger auto-removal when appropriate. As with all new
bugs, there will be at least 30 days before the package is auto-removed.

I have marked the version in unstable as fixing this bug, so if that
version or a later version migrates, this bug will no longer affect
testing. I have also tagged this bug to only affect sid and bullseye, so
it doesn't affect (old-)stable.

If you believe your package is unable to migrate to testing due to
issues beyond your control, don't hesitate to contact the Release Team.

Paul

[1] https://lists.debian.org/debian-devel-announce/2020/02/msg00005.html
[2] https://qa.debian.org/excuses.php?package=r-cran-rmarkdown

Subject: ITP: r-cran-grimport2 -- GNU R importing 'SVG' graphics
Package: wnpp
Owner: Andreas Tille <tille at debian.org>
Severity: wishlist

* Package name    : r-cran-grimport2
  Version         : 0.2
  Upstream Author : Simon Potter, Paul Murrell
* URL             : https://cran.r-project.org/package=grImport2
* License         : GPL-2+
  Programming Lang: GNU R
  Description     : GNU R importing 'SVG' graphics
 Functions for importing external vector images and
 drawing them as part of 'R' plots.  This package is different from the
 'grImport' package because, where that package imports 'PostScript'
 format images, this package imports 'SVG' format images.  Furthermore,
 this package imports a specific subset of 'SVG', so external images
 must be preprocessed using a package like 'rsvg' to produce 'SVG'
 that this package can import.  'SVG' features that are not supported
 by 'R' graphics, e.g., gradient fills, can be imported and then
 exported via the 'gridSVG' package.

Remark: This package is maintained by Debian R Packages Maintainers at
   https://salsa.debian.org/r-pkg-team/r-cran-grimport2

messages.subject_clean: [R-pkg-team] Bug#955739: ITP: r-bioc-sva -- GNU R Surrogate Variable Analysis
messages.body_plain:
Package: wnpp
Severity: wishlist

Subject: ITP: r-bioc-sva -- GNU R Surrogate Variable Analysis
Package: wnpp
Owner: Andreas Tille <tille at debian.org>
Severity: wishlist

* Package name    : r-bioc-sva
  Version         : 3.34.0
  Upstream Author : Jeffrey T. Leek <jtleek at gmail.com>, W. Evan Johnson <wej at bu.edu>,
* URL             : https://bioconductor.org/packages/sva/
* License         : Artistic-2.0
  Programming Lang: GNU R
  Description     : GNU R Surrogate Variable Analysis
 The sva package contains functions for removing batch
 effects and other unwanted variation in high-throughput
 experiment. Specifically, the sva package contains functions
 for the identifying and building surrogate variables for
 high-dimensional data sets. Surrogate variables are covariates
 constructed directly from high-dimensional data (like gene
 expression/RNA sequencing/methylation/brain imaging data) that
 can be used in subsequent analyses to adjust for unknown,
 unmodeled, or latent sources of noise. The sva package can be
 used to remove artifacts in three ways: (1) identifying and
 estimating surrogate variables for unknown sources of variation
 in high-throughput experiments (Leek and Storey 2007 PLoS
 Genetics,2008 PNAS), (2) directly removing known batch
 effects using ComBat (Johnson et al. 2007 Biostatistics) and (3) removing
 batch effects with known control probes (Leek 2014 biorXiv).
 Removing batch effects and using surrogate variables in
 differential expression analysis have been shown to reduce
 dependence, stabilize error rate estimates, and improve
 reproducibility, see (Leek and Storey 2007 PLoS Genetics, 2008
 PNAS or Leek et al. 2011 Nat. Reviews Genetics).

Remark: This package is maintained by Debian R Packages Maintainers at
   https://salsa.debian.org/r-pkg-team/r-bioc-sva

messages.body_plain:
Package: wnpp
Severity: wishlist

Subject: ITP: r-cran-ggpubr -- GNU R ggplot2 based publication ready plots
Package: wnpp
Owner: Andreas Tille <tille at debian.org>
Severity: wishlist

* Package name    : r-cran-ggpubr
  Version         : 0.2.5
  Upstream Author : Alboukadel Kassambara
* URL             : https://cran.r-project.org/package=ggpubr
* License         : GPL-2
  Programming Lang: GNU R
  Description     : GNU R ggplot2 based publication ready plots
 The 'ggplot2' package is excellent and flexible for elegant data
 visualization in R. However the default generated plots requires some
 formatting before it can be send them for publication. Furthermore, to
 customize a 'ggplot', the syntax is opaque and this raises the level of
 difficulty for researchers with no advanced R programming skills.
 'ggpubr' provides some easy-to-use functions for creating and
 customizing 'ggplot2'- based publication ready plots.

Remark: This package is maintained by Debian R Packages Maintainers at
   https://salsa.debian.org/r-pkg-team/r-cran-ggpubr

Subject: ITP: r-cran-gganimate -- GNU R grammar of animated graphics
Package: wnpp
Owner: Andreas Tille <tille at debian.org>

* Package name    : r-cran-gganimate
  Version         : 1.0.5
  Upstream Author : Thomas Lin Pedersen,
* URL             : https://cran.r-project.org/package=gganimate
* License         : MIT
  Programming Lang: GNU R
  Description     : GNU R grammar of animated graphics
 The grammar of graphics as implemented in the 'ggplot2' package has
 been successful in providing a powerful API for creating static
 visualisation. In order to extend the API for animated graphics this package
 provides a completely new set of grammar, fully compatible with 'ggplot2'
 for specifying transitions and animations in a flexible and extensible way.

R/pd_function.R:# Copyright: 2017 University of Utah

Andrew Redd is listed at the Author, but not the copyright holder.  This needs
to be corrected too.

I did not review further than that.

Scott K

messages.subject: [R-pkg-team] r-cran-parsetools_0.1.2-1_amd64.changes REJECTED
messages.body_plain:
Hi Andrew,

I intend to package your R package parsetools for Debian GNU Linux.  Our
ftpmasters have found some inconsistencies in the copyright information.
I've found more files R/*.R that are featuring GPL-3+ explicitly while
in some files an explicit statement is missing.  My naive assumption is
that this is just an oversight you possibly want to fix by bringing all
licenses statements in sync - may be by simply adjusting the License field
inside the DESCRIPTION file?

So far for the upstream issues - thanks for providing parsetools as
Free Software in any case.


Hi Scott,

thanks for spotting the issues.  I've adjusted d/copyright for the
moment as specified in the files explicitly and re-uploaded.

BTW, I'm wondering why licensecheck is failing to report GPL-3 here.
Do you have any better version or any more picky tool I could use to
upload better packages in the first place?

Kind regards and thanks again for your thorough checking

      Andreas.


On Tue, Apr 07, 2020 at 01:00:08AM +0000, Scott Kitterman wrote:
> 
> Unfortunately I am going to have to reject this package.  The license
> information in debian/copyright is incorrect.
> 
> debian/copyright:
> 
> Files: *
> Copyright: 2018-2020 Andrew Redd, R Consortium
> License: GPL-2
> 
> inst/examples/example.R - GPL 3+
> R/parent.R - GPL 3+
> 
> Every file I checked is GPL-3+ (I did not check them all - you need to do
> that).
> 
> Additionally, two files have copyright holders that are not listed:
> 
> R/pd_if.R:# Copyright: 2017 University of Utah
> R/pd_function.R:# Copyright: 2017 University of Utah
> 
> Andrew Redd is listed at the Author, but not the copyright holder.  This needs
> to be corrected too.
> 
> I did not review further than that.
> 
> Scott K
> 
> 
> 
> ===
> 
> Please feel free to respond to this email if you don't understand why
> your files were rejected, or if you upload new files which address our
> concerns.
> 
> 
> _______________________________________________
> R-pkg-team mailing list
> R-pkg-team at alioth-lists.debian.net
> https://alioth-lists.debian.net/cgi-bin/mailman/listinfo/r-pkg-team

-- 
http://fam-tille.de

 for users to customize the graphic parameters such as the font type and
 symbol colors.

Unfortunately the package is not all GPL-2, so I am going to have to reject
the package due to a missing license in debian/copyright:

# extract_tests.R ################################################################

#                                                                                #

# Date: 2017-06-09                                                               #

# Foundation, either version 3 of the License, or (at your option) any later     #

#                                                                                #
# You should have received a copy of the GNU General Public License along with   #
# this program. If not, see http://www.gnu.org/licenses/.                        #
#                                                           

Note: There is a bootstrapping problem here.  testextras needs
r-cran-parsetools to build, but r-cran-parsetools contains generated content
using testextras, so it's not DFSG free for main until testextras is in.

I will review and accept them together to work around this.

Scott K

Please feel free to respond to this email if you don't understand why
your files were rejected, or if you upload new files which address our
concerns.

messages.body_plain:
There are two major issues that I noticed before I gave up.

1.  inst/doc/Specifiying_weights_in_log-rank_comparisons.html is chock full of
sourceless Javascript, which it not allowed in Main (need preferred form of
modification).  That would be enough to require a reject.

2.  vignettes/README.md says `ggsci.css` was borrowed from [`ggsci`](https://
github.com/road2stat/ggsci/tree/master/vignettes) package.  This package is
GPL-2 and ggsci is GPL-3 and has a different copyright.  Please have a look
and see if the GPL-2 and GPL-3 code interact in a way that would cause a
license incompatiblity problem (GPL-2 and GPL-3 are incompatible).  If that's
not a problem, then the license and copyright information for ggsci.css need
to be in debian/copyright.

Scott K
 



===

Please feel free to respond to this email if you don't understand why
your files were rejected, or if you upload new files which address our
concerns.

messages.body_plain:
Package: wnpp

Subject: ITP: r-bioc-tcgabiolinks -- GNU R/Bioconductor package for integrative analysis with GDC data
Package: wnpp
Owner: Andreas Tille <tille at debian.org>
Severity: wishlist

* Package name    : r-bioc-tcgabiolinks
  Version         : 2.14.1
  Upstream Author : Antonio Colaprico,
* URL             : https://bioconductor.org/packages/TCGAbiolinks/
* License         : GPL-3+
  Programming Lang: GNU R
  Description     : GNU R/Bioconductor package for integrative analysis with GDC data
 The aim of TCGAbiolinks is:
  1) facilitate the GDC open-access data retrieval,
  2) prepare the data using the appropriate pre-processing strategies,
  3) provide the means to carry out different standard analyses and
  4) to easily reproduce earlier research results.
 In more detail, the package provides multiple methods for analysis (e.g.,
 differential expression analysis, identifying differentially methylated
 regions) and methods for visualization (e.g., survival plots, volcano plots,
 starburst plots) in order to easily develop complete analysis pipelines.

Remark: This package is maintained by Debian R Packages Maintainers at
   https://salsa.debian.org/r-pkg-team/r-bioc-tcgabiolinks

messages.subject: [R-pkg-team] r-cran-survminer_0.4.6-1_amd64.changes REJECTED
messages.body_plain:
Hi Scott,

thanks again for your thoroug and speedy checking.

On Wed, Apr 08, 2020 at 08:10:11PM +0000, Scott Kitterman wrote:
> 
> There are two major issues that I noticed before I gave up.
> 
> 1.  inst/doc/Specifiying_weights_in_log-rank_comparisons.html is chock full of
> sourceless Javascript, which it not allowed in Main (need preferred form of
> modification).  That would be enough to require a reject.

Arrrgh.  That is removed.  I simply missed that.
 
> 2.  vignettes/README.md says `ggsci.css` was borrowed from [`ggsci`](https://
> github.com/road2stat/ggsci/tree/master/vignettes) package.  This package is
> GPL-2 and ggsci is GPL-3 and has a different copyright.  Please have a look
> and see if the GPL-2 and GPL-3 code interact in a way that would cause a
> license incompatiblity problem (GPL-2 and GPL-3 are incompatible).  If that's
> not a problem, then the license and copyright information for ggsci.css need
> to be in debian/copyright.

This css file is just used to create the documentation.  Its not used
when executing the code.  In principle any other css could be used to
create the docs - than these would look just different than the template
given by a related package.  Since this does not look like any conflict
regarding an interaction of differently licensed code I simply added
another paragraph to d/copyright and re-uploaded.

Thanks again

      Andreas.

-- 
http://fam-tille.de

Hi Scott,

thanks for accepting the package.  I'm addressing your hints in the
source-only upload.

Kind regards

     Andreas.

> #  along with this program; if not, write to the Free Software
> #  Foundation, Inc., 51 Franklin Street, Fifth Floor, Boston, MA  02110-1301, USA.
> 
> Two things, one mandatory, one optional:
> 
> The license requires preservation of the copyright statement, so Vicent Q. Wu
> has to be added to debian/copyright.
> 
> The balance of this package is GPL-3+.  This this is GPL-2+, the current
> debian/copyright infers that Debian will be distributing this only under the
> terms of GPL-3+.  I might be better to add explicit mention of part of this
> file being GPL-2+, but it is not strictly required.
> 
> Scott K

Dear customers,

Do you have any new projects ? thanks.

Trust can only come with time and experience of dealing with Dare-Fly.

the Debian packaged version of svglite received a bug report[1] about a

r-cran-svglite/tests(master) $ LC_ALL=C R --no-save < testthat.R

> library(svglite)
> 
> test_check("svglite")
-- 1. Error: symbol font family is 'Symbol' (@test-text-fonts.R#30)  -----------
StartTag: invalid element name [68]

 1. svglite::xmlSVG(...)

Execution halted



Do you have any hint how to fix this test?  May be its some missing
font package we should add to the dependencies?

Kind regards

      Andreas.

messages.body_plain:
Package: wnpp
Severity: wishlist

Subject: ITP: r-cran-optimalcutpoints -- Computing Optimal Cutpoints in Diagnostic Tests
Package: wnpp
Owner: Steffen Moeller <moeller at debian.org>
Severity: wishlist

* Package name    : r-cran-optimalcutpoints
  Version         : 1.1
  Upstream Author : Monica Lopez-Raton, Maria Xose Rodriguez-Alvarez
* URL             : https://cran.r-project.org/package=OptimalCutpoints
* License         : GPL-2
  Programming Lang: GNU R
  Description     : Computing Optimal Cutpoints in Diagnostic Tests
 Computes optimal cutpoints for diagnostic tests or continuous markers.
 Various approaches for selecting optimal cutoffs have been implemented,
 including methods based on cost-benefit analysis and diagnostic test
 accuracy measures (Sensitivity/Specificity, Predictive Values and
 Diagnostic Likelihood Ratios). Numerical and graphical output for all
 methods is easily obtained.

Remark: This package is maintained by Debian R Packages Maintainers at
   https://salsa.debian.org/r-pkg-team/r-cran-optimalcutpoints

messages.subject_clean: [R-pkg-team] Bug#958705: ITP: r-cran-dqrng -- Fast Pseudo Random Number Generators
messages.body_plain:
Package: wnpp
Severity: wishlist

Subject: ITP: r-cran-dqrng -- Fast Pseudo Random Number Generators
Package: wnpp
Owner: Steffen Moeller <moeller at debian.org>
Severity: wishlist

* Package name    : r-cran-dqrng
  Version         : 0.2.1
  Upstream Author : Copyright: (FIXME: year)-2019 Ralf Stubner,
* URL             : https://cran.r-project.org/package=dqrng
* License         : AGPL-3
  Programming Lang: GNU R
  Description     : Fast Pseudo Random Number Generators
 Several fast random number generators are provided as C++
 header only libraries: The PCG family by O'Neill (2014
 <https://www.cs.hmc.edu/tr/hmc-cs-2014-0905.pdf>) as well as
 Xoroshiro128+ and Xoshiro256+ by Blackman and Vigna (2018
 <arXiv:1805.01407>). In addition fast functions for generating random
 numbers according to a uniform, normal and exponential distribution
 are included. The latter two use the Ziggurat algorithm originally
 proposed by Marsaglia and Tsang (2000, <doi:10.18637/jss.v005.i08>).
 These functions are exported to R and as a C++ interface and are
 enabled for use with the default 64 bit generator from the PCG family,
 Xoroshiro128+ and Xoshiro256+ as well as the 64 bit version of the 20 rounds
 Threefry engine (Salmon et al., 2011 <doi:10.1145/2063384.2063405>) as
 provided by the package 'sitmo'.

Remark: This package is maintained by Debian R Packages Maintainers at
   https://salsa.debian.org/r-pkg-team/r-cran-dqrng

* License         : GPL-2

  Description     : Visualization of Functional Analysis Data

 representation of functional analysis data. It combines and integrates
 omics data derived from expression and functional annotation enrichment

 information for the molecules in a given set of categories (circle plot,
 chord plot, cluster plot, Venn diagram, heatmap).

messages.body_plain:
Package: wnpp

Subject: ITP: r-bioc-dexseq -- Inference of differential exon usage in RNA-Seq
Package: wnpp
Owner: Michael R. Crusoe <michael.crusoe at gmail.com>
Severity: wishlist

* Package name    : r-bioc-dexseq
  Version         : 1.32.0
  Upstream Author : Simon Anders <sanders at fs.tum.de> and Alejandro Reyes
* URL             : https://bioconductor.org/packages/DEXSeq/
* License         : GPL-3+
  Programming Lang: GNU R
  Description     : Inference of differential exon usage in RNA-Seq
 The package is focused on finding differential exon usage
 using RNA-seq exon counts between samples with different
 experimental designs. It provides functions that allows the
 user to make the necessary statistical tests based on a model
 that uses the negative binomial distribution to estimate the
 variance between biological replicates and generalized linear
 models for testing. The package also provides functions for the
 visualization and exploration of the results.

Remark: This package is maintained by Debian R Packages Maintainers at
   https://salsa.debian.org/r-pkg-team/r-bioc-dexseq
